sources.title: IGNOU: Early Historic Societies, Unit 10, Early Tamil Society
sources.note: University course, Unit 10: Sources and Chronology, pages 108 to 109; Polity, page 114. Downloaded and read. Sangam works are bardic texts with problematic internal chronology. Cholas centered on Kaveri delta, Uraiyur and Puhar; Cheras and Pandyas distinct. All units in this block grouped as one work.

sources.title: K. Rajan and R. Sivanantham: Inscribed Potsherds of Tamil Nadu, Graffiti and Tamiḻi, volume 1 (2026)
sources.note: Government Department of Archaeology catalogue, printed pages 201 to 203. Downloaded original PDF from Internet Archive item tamildigitallibrary.062969. Page 202/PDF 241 visually verified. Exact scholarly transcription is antāṉaṉ of Mūlāṉpēdu, with interpretation explicitly probable. Later building phases are excluded. Speculative wider Indus-script continuity claims in the book are not adopted.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Indian Archaeology 1965 to 1966, A Review
sources.note: Printed page 26, item 37, Excavation at Uraiyur. Original government report indexed full entry read; direct report download unsuccessful. Period I first century BCE to fourth CE has pottery, floors and postholes; Period II fourth to sixth/seventh centuries has flood and waterlogging evidence. Do not move Period II ornaments or flooding into 200 to 300 CE.

sources.title: K. V. Soundara Rajan: Kaveripattinam Excavations 1963 to 1973, ASI Memoir 90 (1994)
sources.note: Original government excavation report downloaded from Commons mirror and selected pages visually read. Printed pages 23 to 25/PDF 38 to 40: early historic ring well, Vanagiri sluice and Kilayur wooden/brick wharf. Printed page 130/PDF 149: later monastic occupation and multi-phase port landscape. Dates are broad and some installations precede or follow atlas century; no attribution to a named king without inscription.

sources.title: Paṭṭiṉappālai, original Tamil with translation and notes by Vaidehi Herbert
sources.note: Translator’s complete primary text and translation read directly. Lines 20 to 27: wealthy household image; 40 to 50: kitchens; 78 to 83: fishing homes; 94 to 105: bathing and play. All mirrors and translations of this poem conservatively treated as one underlying work. Literary representations explicitly identified; no date for a surviving ancient manuscript asserted.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Department of Archaeology: Tamil-Brahmi Script
sources.note: Official original indexed page checked; direct fetch failed. Regional distribution and objects bearing writing; source dates Early/Late Tamil-Brahmi broadly third century BCE to third century CE. Universal claims that all modern scripts derive from Brahmi excluded. No cave inscription assigned to a Chola ruler merely from language.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct from chola-empire. Existing medieval card covers Vijayalaya, Rajaraja, Rajendra and later institutions; do not alias or backdate those claims.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Single 200 to 300 CE polygon bounds 74.778 to 80.319 E, 8.027 to 13.528 N. Point tests: Uraiyur, Madurai, Karur and Kanyakumari inside; Puhar and Vanagiri outside. Public opening and port section explicitly disclose coastal omissions and overextended regional attribution.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: antāṉaṉ, scholarly Roman copy, probable Brahmana. Rajan and Sivanantham 2026 volume 1 page 202/PDF 241. Both underlined n characters are U+1 E 49, verified visually and against original PDF text. Not substituted retroflex ṇ. No guessed Brahmi glyphs.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Poetry kept separate from excavated objects; no mass literacy or healthcare system inferred. Early and later Uraiyur phases separated. Puhar timber phase is earlier than map window; monastic phase later. No exact fall year, invented founder, or succession geometry asserted.
